name: object-images-contract-spec
doc: Data contract for the object_images table containing image URLs and metadata for museum objects, including primary images, additional images, and creation timestamps.

object_id.description: Identifying number for each artwork (unique, can be used as key field)

primary_image.description: URL to the primary image of an object (JPEG)

additional_images.description: Array of URLs to additional JPEG images of the object

created_at.description: Timestamp when this record was created in the database

metadataApplicationProfile.title: Museum SQL prompt metadata application profile
metadataApplicationProfile.purpose: Describe the meaning and use of metadata in the fixed museum SQL exercise. This local application profile is not a Linked Art conformance claim.

sources.title: Linked Art model introduction
sources.use: Distinguish physical objects from conceptual works and digital representations.

sources.title: Linked Art required vocabulary: collection items and artworks
sources.use: Collection membership does not establish artwork classification. This exercise explicitly uses a local object-record counting convention.

elements.definition: Treat NULL and empty or whitespace-only text as missing. For populated text, use NULLIF(BTRIM(column), '') IS NOT NULL.
Join museum tables on object_id. Count artworks at the object_id grain; do not multiply counts through expansions.
Public domain means is_public_domain IS TRUE. An image URL alone does not establish public-domain status.
Return only requested columns in their requested order. Follow requested sorting and tie breakers; do not add a LIMIT unless requested.

In this exercise, artwork means one museum object record identified by object.object_id. This is a local counting convention, not evidence that every collection item is classified as an artwork in Linked Art. Do not count images, tags, or conceptual works as extra objects.

Artist name is object.artist_display_name; title is object.title; department is object_gallery_info.department; culture is object_history.culture; classification and medium are in object_physical_properties; primary image URL is object_images.primary_image; public-domain status is object_copyright.is_public_domain. Use the stated field, not a related label or proxy.

For populated text use NULLIF(BTRIM(column), '') IS NOT NULL; for missing text use NULLIF(BTRIM(column), '') IS NULL. Combine conditions with AND or OR exactly as asked. For object counts count object IDs, not distinct field values. For distinct values use DISTINCT; for counts per category GROUP BY that category. Join only the tables needed, using qualified object_id columns. Preserve the requested row grain and avoid extra columns.

The query tool returns columns and rows. Submit only its complete rows array as the final rows value, preserving numbers, strings, NULLs, duplicates, and row order. Do not return SQL, column names, explanations, or numbers remembered from other questions.

metadataApplicationProfile.approved_instructions: Translate the question into one PostgreSQL SELECT using the supplied schema. Resolve the entity, field, missing-value rule, aggregation, and requested output before writing SQL. Use the semantic rules below. After the query succeeds, copy its result rows exactly into the final answer; do not recalculate or substitute values. No retries are allowed.
metadataApplicationProfile.scope: Checks prompt declarations, approved instructions, and rendered rule definitions against the approved MAP. It does not prove model compliance or full Linked Art conformance.

additionalProfiles.title: Workshop sculpture category membership
additionalProfiles.purpose: A proposed local definition for a separate sculpture-counting exercise. This explicit category group is not a claim that every sculpture in the museum is classified here, or that the source conforms to Linked Art.
additionalProfiles.question: How many sculptures are in our sample?
additionalProfiles.approved_instructions: Answer the workshop question: How many sculptures are in our sample? Use the supplied sculpture category definition to select object records from object_physical_properties, count distinct object_id values, and return the count. Preserve the approved category membership and report unclassified records as unknown when discussing coverage.

sources.use: The 17 listed source labels explicitly name sculpture. Their membership is proposed for review and is not expanded by substring matching at runtime.

additionalProfiles.scope: Count one object_id for each record with a listed classification. NULL, empty, and space-only classifications remain unknown; other labels are outside this local count, not declarations that those objects cannot be sculptures. No equivalence with a Linked Art concept or AAT identifier is asserted.

elements.definition: For this workshop, a sculpture is one museum object record whose object_physical_properties.classification, after trimming surrounding spaces, exactly matches a listed category. Count each object_id once. Use the complete explicit list below; do not replace it with classification = 'Sculpture', a substring search, or a guess from material, title, or object name.
